messages.subject: Generate item characteristic curves from IFA (lavaan)
messages.subject_clean: Generate item characteristic curves from IFA (lavaan)
messages.body_plain:
This is not a mirt question per se (I hope that's okay). I fit an item factor analysis model in lavaan using 3-point likert-type data. The model is a two-parameter (i.e., thresholds and factor loadings) graded response model that uses a WLSMV estimator and theta parameterization.

I'd like to generate item characteristic curves for the items from the model. I was thinking the most straightforward way to do this might be to translate the item parameters from an IFA metric (i.e., threshold and factor loading) to the metric of traditional IRT parameters (i.e., difficulty and discrimination, respectively). However, I'm not sure how to convert them from the IFA metric to the IRT metric. Any suggestions how to do this (or, ultimately, how to create item characteristic curves from this model) would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance!
-Isaac

messages.subject_clean: NaN model fit stats for large datasets?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for your excellent package! I've been using it for years and finally have an issue...

I seem to be running into an issue getting model fit stats (including log-likelihood) when modeling large datasets...I thought it was just a recent bug, but I've tried downgrading (back to v1.43). This is across multiple large datasets (it doesn't appear to be an issue with the data, just with the number of items: below, 820 items works; 830 does not (138 participants -- not a huge matrix). Is this a known memory issue? Should I be worried that the models are not actually fitting? Happens with Rasch, 2PL, 3PL..

> mod_1pl <- mirt(d_mat[,1:820], 1, itemtype='Rasch', verbose=TRUE,
+                    technical=list(NCYCLES=4000),
+                    prior=list(d = 'norm(0, 4)'))
Iteration: 44, Log-Lik: -47626.457, Max-Change: 0.00010
> mod_1pl

Call:

    technical = list(NCYCLES = 4000), prior = list(d = "norm(0, 4)"))

Seems to fit, but doesn't print correctly (also NaN in mod_1pl@Fit and logLik(mod_1pl)):
